external_entities.name: user's browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser that communicates with the web application.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.
external_entities.notes: The text does not separately describe the user as an actor; the browser is the named communicating entity.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application that receives browser traffic and places jobs onto the message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue
processes.notes: The web application reads its configuration, including queue credentials.

processes.name: background worker
processes.description: A background process that picks jobs from the message queue and performs the work.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.
processes.notes: The background worker reads its configuration, including database credentials.

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue onto which the web application puts jobs and from which the background worker picks them up.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue, and a background worker process picks them up
data_stores.notes: The text does not state what kind of data the jobs contain.

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database read and written by the background worker and used to keep application log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database. The database is also where we keep the application's log records.
data_stores.notes: The text does not specify the classification of the database contents beyond application log records.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: The configuration store containing the web application's settings and queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config
data_stores.notes: This config store holds the web application's queue credentials.

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: The configuration store containing the worker's settings and database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config
data_stores.notes: This config store holds the worker's database credentials.

data_flows.name: browser traffic
data_flows.description: Traffic from the user's browser to the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.
data_flows.notes: The text says this is the one link marked as encrypted.

data_flows.name: enqueue jobs
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_flows.notes: The text does not say how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: pick up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.
data_flows.notes: The text does not say how the worker accesses or authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: read and write database
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.notes: The text does not say how the worker authenticates to the database.
data_flows.data_description: database records and application log records

data_flows.name: read settings
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from its configuration store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config
data_flows.notes: The settings include the web application's queue credentials.

data_flows.name: read settings
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings from its configuration store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: … the worker has a worker config.
data_flows.notes: The settings include the worker's database credentials.

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public network outside the system's network through which the user's browser communicates with the web application.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.
trust_boundaries.notes: The browser is described as sitting outside our network.

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The network tier in which the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier.

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The network tier containing the message queue, background worker, and database behind the web tier.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because a user's browser communicates with it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the user's browser talks to the web application across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker presents a non-web interface because it is described as a background worker process that picks up jobs and does work rather than serving a web application.
assumptions.basis: The source describes it as a background worker process that picks jobs from a message queue.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config is confidential because it holds queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web application config holds the credentials the process needs, including the web application's queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config is confidential because it holds database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the worker config holds the credentials the process needs, including the worker's database credentials.
